shabbatTonight.title: Shabbat Tonight
shabbatTonight.subtitle: Hoshana Rabbah • entering Shabbat • approaching Simchat Torah
shabbatTonight.reading: This Shabbat stands at a threshold. We are finishing the annual Torah cycle and preparing to begin again with Bereshit. The Torah ends with Moses looking toward a future he will not personally enter, while Genesis immediately returns us to the words “In the beginning.” Jewish learning does not treat finishing as an ending. We complete the Torah and begin it again because familiar words can reveal something new when we return to them with new experience.
shabbatTonight.torah: Read or recall Deuteronomy 34 alongside Genesis 1:1. Notice the movement from Moses’ final view of the Promised Land to the creation of the world.
questions: Why do you think Jewish tradition moves so quickly from the end of Torah back to the beginning?
What is something you understand differently now than you did the last time you encountered it?
shabbatTonight.hebrew: Listen tonight for words you have been learning: Baruch • Eloheinu • Melech • ha-olam • lechem • ha-aretz.
shabbatTonight.closing: As we enter Shabbat, carry one idea from the week with you: Jewish learning is cyclical. We return, reread and discover again.

weeks.label: Week 1
weeks.theme: Bereshit — What does it mean to be responsible?
weeks.shabbat: Cain asks, “Am I my brother’s keeper?” What answer does the rest of Torah seem to give?

tasks.title: Lunch Study — What is kavanah?
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read about kavanah, the Jewish idea of intention in prayer and mitzvot. Ask: What changes when I understand the words I am saying rather than simply reciting them?

tasks.title: Monday Drive — Being Human (Bereshit)
tasks.detail: 14 min • Rabbi Micah Streiffer reads Adam and Eve not mainly as a story of sin and punishment, but as a story about what it means to be human. Listen for how choice, vulnerability and responsibility emerge in the first human story.

tasks.title: One-sentence takeaway
tasks.detail: After the drive, finish this sentence: “Being my brother’s keeper means…”

tasks.title: Lunch Study — Bereshit: creation and human purpose
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read Genesis 1:1–2:3 slowly. Notice repetition: God sees, separates, names, blesses and rests. Ask what kind of world this structure describes.

tasks.title: Shema: listen before reading
tasks.detail: Work with Shema = hear/listen and Yisrael = Israel. Say the opening slowly several times: Shema Yisrael, Adonai Eloheinu, Adonai Echad.

tasks.title: Tuesday Drive — The Nighttime Shema
tasks.detail: 7 min • Rabbi Denise Eger shares a simple, personal practice of reciting the Shema at bedtime. Listen once, then replay it or spend the rest of the drive repeating Shema Yisrael slowly and thinking about what it means to truly listen.

tasks.title: Connect familiar words
tasks.detail: Notice Eloheinu from the blessing formula inside the Shema. The goal is recognition, not memorizing every letter yet.

tasks.title: Lunch Study — Pirkei Avot 1:2
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read the Mishnah that says the world stands on Torah, divine service, and acts of lovingkindness. Consider which of the three is strongest in your Jewish life right now and which needs growth.

tasks.title: Wednesday Drive — Ta Shma (Hadar)
tasks.detail: Use Hadar’s actual Apple Podcasts feed, Ta Shma. This is their beit midrash podcast with lectures and Torah learning. Choose the assigned episode shown in Apple Podcasts; we’ll use it for rabbinic reasoning rather than the unavailable Five-Minute Mishnah.

tasks.title: Listen for rabbinic reasoning
tasks.detail: As you listen, identify one textual question, one interpretation, and one idea you would want to discuss with someone else.

tasks.title: Weekly Rabbi Sacks — The Blame Game
tasks.detail: Covenant & Conversation Family Edition • Bereishit 5787. Read Rabbi Sacks’ teaching on Adam and Chava, blame, mistakes, family tension and the responsibility to be honest when we fail. Use the discussion questions at the end as your reflection.

tasks.title: Lunch Study — Why Shabbat has two meanings
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read how Torah connects Shabbat both to Creation and to liberation from Egypt. Ask why Judaism makes rest both a spiritual idea and a question of human freedom.

tasks.title: Genesis 1:1–2:3
tasks.detail: Read the first creation account. Look for repeated words and patterns rather than trying to master the whole chapter.

tasks.title: Peshat question
tasks.detail: What does the structure of the seven days suggest the text wants you to notice about creation, order and rest?

tasks.title: Lunch Study — Shabbat as a sanctuary in time
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read Abraham Joshua Heschel’s idea that Judaism sanctifies time, not only places. While traveling, ask what it could mean to create sacred time without being at home.

tasks.title: Bereshit in one idea
tasks.detail: This Shabbat begins the Torah cycle with creation, human choice, Cain and Abel, and the first questions about responsibility.

tasks.title: Simple Shabbat intention
tasks.detail: No full study session required while traveling. Before Shabbat, say the Shema slowly and notice Shema, Yisrael and Eloheinu.

tasks.title: Shabbat question
tasks.detail: Cain asks, “Am I my brother’s keeper?” What answer do you think Torah wants us to give?

tasks.title: Lunch Study — Cain and responsibility
tasks.detail: Optional travel reading • Read Genesis 4:1–16 and focus on God’s questions to Cain: “Where is your brother?” and Cain’s response. Connect it to Monday’s Seven Minute Torah episode.

tasks.title: Cain and Abel — Genesis 4:1–16
tasks.detail: Read only this focused section if you have time. Notice what God asks Cain before and after Abel’s death.

tasks.title: Return to Monday’s podcast
tasks.detail: Does the Torah itself answer Cain’s question directly, or does it make the reader responsible for answering it?

tasks.title: Lunch Study — Rest and renewal
tasks.detail: Optional travel reading • Read about menuchah as more than inactivity: Shabbat rest as peace, wholeness and a different relationship with the created world.

tasks.title: Beginning Cheshvan
tasks.detail: Rosh Chodesh marks the beginning of a new Hebrew month. Cheshvan follows the festival-heavy month of Tishrei; consider what practice you want to carry from the holidays into ordinary time.

tasks.title: One intention
tasks.detail: Choose one small Jewish practice to continue this month: a blessing, Shema, weekly Torah, or a Shabbat question.

days.minutes: Out of town / return • light review

tasks.title: Lunch Study — Prayer 101
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read an overview of Jewish prayer as both communication with God and connection with the Jewish people. Notice the balance between fixed liturgy and personal meaning.

tasks.title: Hebrew recognition review
tasks.detail: Without adding new vocabulary, review Baruch, Atah, Eloheinu, Melech, ha-olam, Shema and Yisrael.

tasks.title: Close the week
tasks.detail: Which idea stayed with you most: creation, rest, human choice, responsibility, or beginning again?

weeks.label: Week 2
weeks.theme: Noach — From personal responsibility to moral courage
weeks.description: A manageable catch-up week: carry forward key Bereishit lessons, then explore Noach and what it means to speak up.

tasks.title: Carryover — Rabbi Sacks: The Blame Game (Bereishit 5787)
tasks.detail: 15 min • Missed weekend priority. Read the current-year Family Edition; reflect on one situation where an explanation became an excuse.

tasks.title: Carryover — Cain and Abel (Genesis 4:1–16)
tasks.detail: 5–10 min optional • Focus on 'Am I my brother's keeper?' Skip if time is short.

tasks.title: Hebrew — Shema and blessing formula
tasks.detail: 5 min • Recognize Shema Yisrael, Baruch atah Adonai and Eloheinu; say each aloud.

tasks.title: Question
tasks.detail: What is the difference between giving context and avoiding responsibility?

days.focus: Noach: what makes a righteous person?

tasks.title: Lunch Study — Noach: righteousness in his generation
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read Genesis 6:9–22 and identify what the Torah praises about Noach.

tasks.title: Rashi on Genesis 6:9
tasks.detail: 5 min optional • Compare two ways to interpret 'in his generation'.

tasks.title: Hebrew — Noach / tzaddik
tasks.detail: 5 min • נֹחַ (Noach, Noah) and צַדִּיק (tzaddik, righteous person).

tasks.title: Question
tasks.detail: Is it enough to behave well yourself when others around you are doing harm?

tasks.title: Wednesday Drive — Noach discussion podcast
tasks.detail: Listen in the car • Brisk podcast for today's Noach learning and reflection.

days.focus: From personal goodness to moral courage

tasks.title: Weekly Rabbi Sacks — Taking a Stand (Noach 5787)
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • This year's Family Edition. Consider when a good person must speak up for others.

tasks.title: Optional deeper essay — A Story of Heaven and Earth
tasks.detail: Optional • Rabbi Sacks' featured 5787 Covenant & Conversation essay, on the Tower of Babel and society.

tasks.title: Hebrew — Shabbat blessing review
tasks.detail: 5 min • Read the first line of Kiddush or Hamotzi aloud.

tasks.title: Question
tasks.detail: When does staying silent become a choice with moral consequences?

tasks.title: Lunch Study — History and Development of Shabbat
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • My Jewish Learning: trace Shabbat from the Torah through rabbinic law, Kiddush, medieval poetry, and modern Jewish practice.

tasks.title: This Week's Torah — Noach (Genesis 6:9–11:32)
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read the weekly portion, focusing on Noah's righteousness, his silence, and God's covenant. If short on time, focus on Genesis 6:9–22 and 9:8–17.

tasks.title: Lunch Study — The rainbow covenant
tasks.detail: 15 min • Read Genesis 9:8–17; notice who is included in God's covenant.

tasks.title: Shabbat preparation — candles, Kiddush, Hamotzi
tasks.detail: 5 min • Practice the familiar blessings; use the existing full table guide for prayer text.

tasks.title: Shabbat table question
tasks.detail: How can our family move from being good individually to helping others?

tasks.title: Torah portion — Noach (Genesis 6:9–11:32)
tasks.detail: Optional • Read selected passages or explore the full portion.

tasks.title: Shabbat reflection
tasks.detail: What would it mean to take a stand kindly, rather than self-righteously?

tasks.title: Pirkei Avot 1:2 — what sustains the world?
tasks.detail: 10 min • Revisit this missed rabbinic text: Torah, service, and acts of kindness.

tasks.title: Review
tasks.detail: Recall one idea from Bereishit and one from Noach. No need to complete every missed assignment.

tasks.title: Lunch Study — Tower of Babel
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read Genesis 11:1–9 and ask what goes wrong when human ambition loses humility.

tasks.title: Hebrew review — Shema, Hamotzi, Noach, tzaddik
tasks.detail: 5 min • Recognize or pronounce each without looking at transliteration first.

tasks.title: Weekly takeaway
tasks.detail: How did the week's learning change your understanding of responsibility?

weeks.label: Week 3 — Lech Lecha
weeks.theme: From Noah's righteousness to Abraham's courage
weeks.description: Daily Torah and ethical readings, current-year Rabbi Sacks 5787, a direct Apple Podcasts episode, and a printable Friday-night table guide.

tasks.title: Torah — Genesis 12:1–9: Leave the familiar
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Trace the three things Abram leaves behind. What does it cost to follow a calling without knowing the destination?

tasks.title: Drive — Rabbi Sacks: The Courage Not to Conform
tasks.detail: 9 min • Direct Apple Podcasts episode; consider how Abraham differs from Noah.

tasks.title: Daily Hebrew — לֶךְ־לְךָ (Lech lecha)
tasks.detail: 5–10 min • Go forth. Practice ל (lamed), ך (final kaf), and the root ה־ל־ך (to go/walk). Read לֶךְ slowly, then לְךָ. Say the phrase three times and find it in Genesis 12:1.

tasks.title: Rabbi Sacks — Four Dimensions of the Journey
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Explore how leaving familiar surroundings can be a journey toward one's moral self.

tasks.title: Torah — Genesis 12:10–20: Sarai in Egypt
tasks.detail: Reflect on Abram's fear and Sarai's vulnerability. Do not treat the patriarchs as morally flawless.

tasks.title: Daily Hebrew — אֶרֶץ (Eretz)
tasks.detail: 5–10 min • Land. Practice א (alef), ר (resh), ץ (final tsadi). Identify אֶרֶץ in Genesis 12:1; contrast אַרְצְךָ (your land). Read aloud five times.

tasks.title: Rabbi Sacks 5787 Family Edition — The Constant Journey
tasks.detail: Priority 15–20 min • This year's Lech Lecha Family Edition. Connect uncertainty, Jewish resilience, and the responsibility to speak up against antisemitism.

tasks.title: Torah — Genesis 13:5–18: Conflict with Lot
tasks.detail: Notice Abram's peaceful resolution of conflict and the responsibilities of family and leadership.

tasks.title: Daily Hebrew — בְּרִית (Brit)
tasks.detail: 5–10 min • Covenant. Practice ב (bet), ר (resh), י (yod), ת (tav). Find בְּרִית in Genesis 17:7; explain in one sentence how covenant differs from a simple promise.

days.focus: Preparing a Shabbat of courage and blessing

tasks.title: Rabbi Sacks 5787 — The Heroism of Ordinary Life
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read the current-year main essay about Abraham and the extraordinary power of ordinary moral choices.

tasks.title: Friday Dinner — Lech Lecha Shabbat Table Guide (PDF)
tasks.detail: Friday dinner discussion guide in the app: Noah to Abraham, moral courage, Rabbi Sacks, and family questions. Full printable two-page siddur-style PDF is also provided in this chat.

tasks.title: Torah — Genesis 12:1–3: Become a blessing
tasks.detail: Discuss: how can our family be a source of blessing beyond our own home?

tasks.title: Daily Hebrew — בְּרָכָה (Berakhah)
tasks.detail: 5–10 min • Blessing. Practice בְּ (b), רָ (ra), כָ (kha), ה (h). Say בְּרָכָה and compare בָּרוּךְ (barukh) in the Shabbat blessings. Read Genesis 12:2.

tasks.title: Weekly Torah — Lech Lecha (Genesis 12:1–17:27)
tasks.detail: Read selected passages or the full parashah. Focus on journey, Sarai, Lot, Hagar, Ishmael, and covenant.

tasks.title: Shabbat reflection — Genesis 15:1–6
tasks.detail: God tells Abram not to fear; explore trust in the face of uncertainty.

tasks.title: Daily Hebrew — אֱמוּנָה (Emunah)
tasks.detail: 5–10 min • Faithfulness / trust. Practice א (alef), מ (mem), ו (vav), נ (nun), ה (heh). This is a thematic vocabulary word, not a word from Genesis 12:1. Relate it to וְהֶאֱמִן (he trusted/believed) in Genesis 15:6.

days.focus: The people left out of the heroic narrative

tasks.title: Torah — Genesis 16:1–16: Hagar and Ishmael
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Read Hagar's experience as a person with her own voice and suffering. What does the story ask us to notice about power?

tasks.title: Reform Torah commentary — Lech Lecha
tasks.detail: Consider contemporary Jewish interpretations of Abraham and Sarah's family.

tasks.title: Daily Hebrew — שָׁלוֹם (Shalom)
tasks.detail: 5–10 min • Peace / wholeness. Practice שׁ (shin), ל (lamed), ו (vav), ם (final mem). Say Shalom Aleichem and identify שָׁלוֹם in the Friday-night song. Write the word once from memory.

tasks.title: Torah — Genesis 17:1–27: Names and covenant
tasks.detail: 15–20 min • Why do Abram and Sarai receive new names? What changes when a personal calling becomes an intergenerational obligation?

tasks.title: Preview — Genesis 18:16–33: Abraham speaks up
tasks.detail: Bridge to Vayera: compare Abraham's argument for Sodom with Noah's silence.

tasks.title: Daily Hebrew — שֵׁם (Shem)
tasks.detail: 5–10 min • Name. Practice שׁ (shin) and ם (final mem). Read שֵׁם, then compare Abram/Abraham and Sarai/Sarah in Genesis 17:5,15. What changes when a name changes?

prayers.title: Blessing Formula
prayers.hebrew: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם
prayers.translit: Baruch atah Adonai, Eloheinu melech ha-olam.
prayers.english: Blessed are You, Adonai our God, Sovereign of the universe.
prayers.words: Baruch = blessed • Atah = You • Eloheinu = our God • Melech = sovereign/king • Ha-olam = the universe/world

prayers.title: Hamotzi
prayers.hebrew: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם׃ הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ
prayers.translit: Baruch atah Adonai, Eloheinu melech ha-olam; hamotzi lechem min ha-aretz.
prayers.english: Blessed are You, Adonai our God, Sovereign of the universe, who brings forth bread from the earth.
prayers.words: Lechem = bread • Min = from • Ha-aretz = the earth

learning.title: Torah & Commentary
learning.description: Start with the text, notice the problem, then ask what the commentator is trying to explain.

items.title: Genesis 1:1
items.detail: Read Bereshit slowly. What questions arise before consulting commentary?

items.title: Rashi on Genesis 1:1
items.detail: Ask the recurring question: What problem did Rashi see that required explanation?

items.title: Deuteronomy 34
items.detail: Read Torah’s ending beside its beginning. Notice what Moses leaves unfinished.

learning.title: Mishnah & Talmud
learning.description: Learn in small units and focus on how rabbinic reasoning works.

items.title: Pirkei Avot
items.detail: A welcoming entry into Mishnah: short teachings that reward slow reading and discussion.

items.title: How to read an argument
items.detail: Identify the claim, question, disagreement, evidence, counterexample and resolution. The goal is to follow the reasoning, not rush to an answer.

learning.title: Spiritual Practice
learning.description: Connect study to prayer, Shabbat and ordinary life.

items.title: Blessing awareness
items.detail: When you encounter a blessing, notice the repeated formula before focusing on the words that make this blessing unique.

items.title: Shabbat reflection
items.detail: Carry one question from the week to the Friday table instead of trying to summarize everything you learned.
